reason: This text from Exodus 3-4 describes God hearing the cries of the suffering Israelites in Egypt (וְאֶת־ צַעֲקָתָם שָׁמַעְתִּי - 'I have heard their cry') and witnessing their oppression (וְאֶת־ הַלַּחַץ אֲשֶׁר מִצְרַיִם לֹחֲצִים אֹתָם - 'the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them'). Rather than attributing their suffering to their own fault, God explicitly takes compassion on them, identifies Himself as their God, and commits to their deliverance: 'וָאֵרֵד לְהַצִּילוֹ' (I will deliver them). No leader in this narrative blames the people for their suffering; instead, God affirms their grievances and promises redemption.
